name: Testament of Berengarius de Bulbono (AMM 2 II 287)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Charter 2 II 287
description: This charter records the testament of Berengarius de Bulbono. It has not been transcribed, and is made available here for readers interested in consulting his inventory, available elsewhere in the DALME collection.

name: Inventory of Philippus Lamberti (ADBR 355E 48)
description: Philippus Lamberti wrote a testament on 10 March 1390 in which he named as his heirs in equal shares Dulcieta, his wife, and his two sons, Huguetus and Bartholomayretus. Bartholomayretus, and probably Huguetus as well, is the son of a previous wife named Jacmeta. Huguetus has already received his third part, and the remaining 2/3rds are to be shared between Bartholomayretus and Dulcieta. Dulcieta is due her dowry and counter-dowry, amounting to 100 florins. The two agree on an arbitration. Dulcieta chose Petrus Athos, a common friend, and Anthonius Torcati, her brother, to represent her interests in the arbitration. Bartholomayretus, for his part, chooses Laurencius Aycardi, notary, and magister Gaufridus Aycardi, a cooper, who are his cousins.

name: Inventory of Pellegrinus (ADBR 351E 79)
description: This act provides a list of goods that appear to have been given to Anthoneta, widow of Pellegrinus, to compensate her for her dowry of 52 florins. She has an infant son named Horonadetus. Damage to register has caused a number of items to be lost.

name: Inventory of Raymundus Santolhi (ADBR 351E 210)
description: In his testament, Raymundus had named his grandchildren, Monnetus and Peyretus Santolhi, sons of his deceased son Johannes Santolhi, as his heirs for half his goods. Antonius Santolhi, his surviving son, is heir to the other half and also was named as their tutor. Now, Monnetus has reached the age of 20 years, and wants to divide the estate. A division ensues.

name: Inventory of Bernardus de Favacio (ADBR 3 HD H 8)
parent_name: Archives départementales des Bouches-du-Rhône, Charter 3 HD H 8
description: Marquesius de Favacio is the son and heir of the late Bernardus de Favacio. He is also the guardian of Margarideta de Favacio, daughter and heir of the late Aycardus de Favacio, Marquesius's brother and coheir of the estate. The inventory of Bernardus's estate includes many interesting items, such as a set of sheets for use in childbirth. The inventory was originally transcribed by Christine Barnel with corrections and editions by D. Smail. Bibliography: Ripert, Laurent, Christine Barnel, Henri Bresc, Pascal Herberth, and Florence Colin, eds. Matériaux pour l’étude de la vie domestique et de la culture matérielle en Provence aux derniers siècles du Moyen Age. Razo (Nice). Cahiers du centre d’études médiévales de Nice 13. Pp. 53-58. Nice, France: Université de Nice, 1993.

name: Inventory of Benedictus de Tortosa (AMM 1 II 44)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 44
description: Two women appeared in court to announce that the merchant Benedictus de Tortosa has died, leaving his estate to his two heirs. The first is Bartholomea Heleria, the wife of Bertrandus Helie, and sister of Benedictus. The second is Jacmeta, the wife of the late Guillelmus de Tortosa, who is acting as the guardian of her son Andrivetus, the nephew of Benedictus. They request permission to undertake an inventory of the estate. This is an extensive inventory and includes, among other things, an interesting set of armor and weapons.

name: Register of Saint-Esprit (ADBR 1HD E15)
parent_name: Archives départementales des Bouches-du-Rhône, Register 1HD E15
description: To come

name: Inventory of Dulciana Dalbare (AMM FF 501)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 501
description: Dulciana, the wife of Johannes Dalbar, has died, and her heir, Audebertus Desderii, appears in court to undertake the inventory.

name: Auction of the goods of Guillelmus Gayroardi (ADBR 3B 150)
description: Because Guillelmus Gayroardi owed 2 florins and 4 gros to Bertrandus Moro for unpaid rent on a house, Bertrandus had had his goods subjected to an inventory. Both parties now appeared in court and have agreed to have the goods sold at auction in order to avoid further legal action. It is not clear whether the items listed on folio 45v were part of this action or a separate action.

name: Inventory of Jacobus Fornerii (ADBR 3B 145)
description: Bertrandus Morlani, the nephew of Jacobus Fornerii, a peasant or a miller, appear in court. He explains to the judge that his uncle died on the 2nd of May of this year and named Bertrandus as his heir. He wishes to take up the inheritance with benefit of inventory. Although this is a relatively rudimentary estate, it does include a sword and two shields.

name: Inventory of Jacobus Hospitalerii (ADBR 355E 34)
description: Jacobus Hospitalerii was an exceedingly poor man who died alone and friendless in the Black Death or a year or two later. When his abandoned goods were discovered, the court assigned Aragonus de Rabastenco to compile an inventory. This inventory offers an excellent example of the grinding poverty in which some people suffered in a medieval city (note the presence of a single boot).

name: Inventory of Jacobus Albini (ADBR 3B 140)
description: Jacobus had killed Johannes Areati. During the course of the inquest into the killing, an inventory was made of Jacobus’s estate. Unlike post-mortem inventories from the period, even those of relatively middling artisans, this inventory reveals a distinct absence of fine goods, clothing, and even foodstuffs. The inventory was conducted by the notary of the court, accompanied by the sub-viguier and the vice-treasurer of the city

name: Record of an auction (ADBR 3B 150)
description: to come

name: Goods consigned to Salamonetus Boneti and to Regina wife of Cregutus Profachi (ADBR 3B 150)
description: Though no context is provided for this act, it appears to consist of a list of pledges or pawned goods that, for reasons unknown, were being transmitted into the keeping of Salamonetus Boneti and Regina, wife of Cregutus Profachi. It is reasonable to understand this act as equivalent to an inventory of a pawn shop.

name: Inventory of Marques de Favacio (ADBR 3 HD H 12, pièce 7)
parent_name: Archives départementales des Bouches-du-Rhône, Charter 3 HD H 12
description: Lady Catharina de Favacio, widow of the late Marquesius de Favacio, is pregnant, and for this reason, the judge of the lower court of Marseille has come to her house in order to set in motion the inventory of the estate. In the judge's presence, Catharina explains that her husband died not long ago, having left a testament in which he named his wife as the guardian for the couple's children. She wishes to accept the guardianship but requests that Guillelmus de Favacio, the children's paternal uncle, be named as a co-guardian. The inventory includes a transcription of the account book of Marquesius's drapery business, listing dozens of fabrics from all over Europe along with their prices per cane. The inventory was originally transcribed by Christine Barnel, with corrections and additions by D. Smail.Bibliography. Ripert, Laurent, Christine Barnel, Henri Bresc, Pascal Herberth, and Florence Colin, eds. Matériaux pour l’étude de la vie domestique et de la culture matérielle en Provence aux derniers siècles du Moyen Age. Razo (Nice). Cahiers du centre d’études médiévales de Nice 13. Pp. 71-77. Nice, France: Université de Nice, 1993. Barnel, Christine. “Les boutiques des frères Favas: drapiers et draperie à Marseille au XIVe siècle.” Provence Historique 49 (1999): 61-78.

name: Inventory of Johannes Marini (ADBR 351E 152)
description: This act provides very little context for the inventory in contains,  which probably  resulted from  a criminal inquest against Johannes Marini. The objects  listed in this rudimentary estate include a bed, several items of clothing, some weapons, some coins, a goblet, and nine purses.

name: Inventory of Johannes Martini (ADBR 351E 239)
description: This is an inventory of goods owned by Johannes Martini, which he gave into  the keeping of his parents-in-law, Aurionus Royaudi alias Butoni, a crier of the court, and his wife Catherina. The couple promise to restore the goods when asked.

name: Inventory of Bertrandus Pauli (AMM 1 II 44)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 44
description: Alayseta Paule, the daughter of Bertrandus Pauli, a resident of one of Marseille's suburbs, appears in court. She explains to the judge that her father had died in the terrible plague the previous year. He wrote a testament dated the 15th of March, 1348, in which he named Alaseta Paul, his wife, as his heir, and named Alayseta and Johanna, his daughters, as substitute heirs in equal parts in the event of their mother's death. Given the fact that Alayseta was more than a year overdue in requesting an inventory of her father's estate, she felt it necessary to explain the reason for the delay to the judge. What follows is an extraordinary description of the lived experience of the Black Death. Shortly after her father's death, her mother died, as did her sister Johanna and her husband, leaving Alayseta all alone in the world, pregnant, and in anguish and sorrow. Humbly and tearfully, she requested the judge's permission to carry out the inventory. Carefully considering the request, the judge responded that hardly anyone was able to take care of his own business during those difficult times, let alone the business of others, and grants her request. Since the Paul family did their business with the notary Jacobus Aycardi, we have access to the testaments made by Bertrandus Pauli; Hugo Porrate, husband of Alayseta Paule; and Bertrandus's wife Alaseta Paule, mother of Alayseta (see ADBR 355 E 1, folios 51r-53v, 73r-74v, and 75v-77v). In the testament of Bertrandus Pauli, we learn that Alayseta's sister, Johanneta, is "inpotens," meaning physically or mentally incapacitated in some way. Hugo Porrate, in his testament, named as his heir his unborn child, whether a boy or a girl. The Paul family was reasonably well off for a peasant family and are mentioned in about a dozen contracts in this register and elsewhere.

name: Inventory of Franciscus de Serralonga (ADBR 355E 1)
description: This is an inventory of the estate of Franciscus de Serralonga, a cobbler, who died at the very height of the Black Death in April of 1348. The extensive list of his goods includes ceramics from Murcia.

name: Donation of estate of Jacobus Salvage (ADBR 351E 73)
description: The laborer Jacobus Salvage, alias de Valensola, and his wife Monna are citizens and residents of Marseille. They have chosen to make a donation of all their goods to the Hospital of Saint-Jacques de Galicia, and an inventory was drawn up to record the gift.

name: Inventory of Dulcia de Monteolivo (ADBR 5G 775)
description: Dulcia de Monteolivo, the daughter of Giraudus Manentis, wrote a testament on 19 April 1409, in which she named as her  heirs her two daughters, Margarita de Favacio and Laurencia de Monteolivo. Both women are nuns at the monastery of Saint-Sauveur. Margarita is the child of Dulcia's first marriage to Aycardus de Favacio. After Aycardus died, Dulcia married Blaquerie de Monteolivo, who subsequently died. The two nuns, represented by Johannes Mounerii, the procurator for the monastery of Saint-Sauveur, would like to take up the inheritance with benefit of inventory. Because the heirs were members of the church, their request was processed in the episcopal court. The dossier, which opens on 7 May 1409, includes Dulcia's testament, thus providing us with an unusual degree of access to the context. This is one of the wealthiest inventories in the Marseille set.

name: Inventory of Johannes Martini (ADBR 355E 11)
description: Johannes Martini, an urban peasant living in the suburbs, in the carreria Predictorum, has died. A dispute has now arisen over his estate, setting his wife Nicolaua and their daughter Alaysona against his son, Bertrandus Martini. Nicolaua is insisting on the return of her dowry and Alaysona is asking for her share of the inheritance, while Bertrandus wants to insure that he receives all that is coming to him according to the law. Common friends, namely, the draper Jacobus Andree and Petrus Hugonis, serve as arbitrators. In the resulting act, an inventory of Johannes's estate is provided.

name: Dowry of Anthoneta Robaude (ADBR 351E 79)
description: At the time of the wedding between Pellegrinus Rostagni and Anthoneta, daughter of the fisherman Petrus Robaudi, the father of the bride assigned a dowry of 200 l. to his son-in-law. Pellegrinus subsequently died, and the cooper Raymundus Guillelmi was assigned as the guardian for the infant Horonadetus, Pellegrinus's son and heir. Though the act is damaged, it is likely that goods in Pellegrinus's estate were being assessed in value and assigned to Anthoneta as compensation for her dowry.

name: Inventory of Montolina de Monteolivo (AMM 1 II 18)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 18
description: Vivaudetus, age 14 to 15, is the son of the late Blaquerie de Monteolivo and the nephew of the late Montolina, daughter (erroneously described on the first folio as the widow) of the late Blaquerie and wife of the late  Berengarius de Tritis, domicellus. Montolina died, leaving a testament naming Vivaudetus, her nephew, as her heir. The likely genealogy is that a Blaquerie senior had had two children, Blaquerie junior and Montolina, and Blaquerie junior in turn fathered Vivaudetus. The early folios of the record concern the legacies that had been made by Montolina. This is an extremely interesting inventory with a number of unusual objects.

name: Inventory of Marinus de Berra (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: For unknown reasons, Marita Bertrande requests an inventory of the assets of Marinus de Berra. The estate is rudimentary.

name: Inventory of Jacobus Martini (ADBR 1 HD B 56, pièce 7)
parent_name: Archives départementales des Bouches-du-Rhône, Charter 1 HD B 56
description: At the outset of this lengthy charter, we meet Sanxieta, the widow of Jacobus Rodelli, who comes before a judge to  declare that the nobleman Jacobus Martini, her brother, recently died in the city of Salerno, naming her as his universal heir for life. After her death, he wished half of his estate be donated to the Hospital of Saint Esprit, and the other half to the Hospital of Saint-Jacques de Gallice. As the case unfolds, however, we learn that Jacobus Martini appears to have ignored his own wife, Laurencia, whose father engages in a dispute with Sanxieta in order to recover Laurencia's dowry. The inventory, which was drawn up in February, contains a number of interesting items, including the only slave, a woman named Anna, discovered so far in the Marseille collection. The inventory was originally transcribed by Christine Barnel with corrections and additions by D. Smail. Bibliography: Ripert, Laurent, Christine Barnel, Henri Bresc, Pascal Herberth, and Florence Colin, eds. Matériaux pour l’étude de la vie domestique et de la culture matérielle en Provence aux derniers siècles du Moyen Age. Razo (Nice). Cahiers du centre d’études médiévales de Nice 13. Pp. 77-79. Nice, France: Université de Nice, 1993.

name: Inventory of Jacobus de Menas (ADBR 351E 245)
description: Jacobus de Menas has died intestate, leaving his  wife, Catherina (?), and his children Nicolaus, Stephanus, and Margarita. The notary, in the presence of witnesses, undertakes an inventory of the estate. The inventory includes 45 linen shirts  and a further 20 women's shirts with cotton woven in.

name: Inventory of Franciscus Moguerii (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Jacmeta, the widow of Franciscus Moguerii, is seeking to recover her dowry of 110 florins from her husband's insolvent estate. The inventory does not appear to have been carried out room-by-room, and no real estate was found. Total value of goods is 69 florins 3 gros, of which Jacmeta gets 45 fl. and 11 gros. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: Inventory of Colratus Cavallerii (AMM 1 II 21)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 21
description: Beatrix, the wife of the late Colratus Cavallerii, appears in court. She had been the guardian for her three children, Giraudetus, Bartholomeus, and Raymundetus,  but the role has been assigned instead to her new husband, Guillelmus de Vellancio. Guillelmus takes charge of compiling the inventory, beginning with a substantial list of clothes. This inventory is unusually interesting for the number of references to items belonging to Colratus that Beatrix had sold off to pay for funeral expenses or other unstated purposes. It also mentions a garment that was intended to be worn while leaving the baths and describes a garment lined with an unusual fur, sirogrillus, scilicet "choerogryllus" in the DMLBS. The most remarkable objects in this inventory may be two goblets made from the shells of coconuts (nux indie).

name: Inventory of the Sacristy of Accoules (ADBR 351E 98)
description: This short inventory of the sacristy of the church of Notre Dame des Accoules, a parish church located at the very heart of the city of Marseille, includes several interesting items, such as a reliquary containing the blood of Christ.

name: Inventory of Raymundus Cabrerii (ADBR 3B 41)
description: Raymundus is identified as a seaman (marinarius) from Barcelona. He and his wife and mother-in-law, Guillelma Ginhaque, have gone bankrupt and have fled the city (they are described as fugitives). The case includes all the claims of the creditors. The court conducts an inventory of the goods they left behind. Some of the goods belonged to Raymundus; others are identified specifically as in the possession of Secilia and Guillelma. See the inventory of Guillelma Ginhaque in this collection.

name: Inventory of Church of Sainte-Cécile extra muros (ADBR 351E 98)
description: This act records the inventory of the church of the castrum of Sainte-Cécile, located outside the walls of Marseille in a place that is currently not known. The inventory was made by Olivarius, the prior of the church and a beneficed cleric in the cathedral of BM Sedis.

name: Inventory and other acts for Guillelmus Egidii (AMM 1 II 58)
parent_name: Archives Municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 58
description: There has been a dispute between Petrus Egidii, a merchant and citizen of Marseille, the brother and heir of Guillelmus Egidii, and domina Sicilia, the widow of the late Guillelmus. The dispute has been settled by arbitration, and the resolution of the dispute occasioned the making of an inventory of Guillelmus's estate.

name: Inventory of Philipponus Colini (ADBR 5G 771)
description: No context is provided for this inventory of Philipponus Colini, a candler. The inventory is extensive and has a number of interesting features, including many rings and an image of the Virgin Mary made of lead.

name: Inventory of Peyretus Peytamini (ADBR 355E 51)
description: Owing to some words exchanged between Bernardus Peytamini, mariner, and his wife Sileta on the one hand, and Peyretus Peytamini, their son, and his wife Martona, on the other, Peyretus and Martona with their children have chosen to leave Bernardus’s house. Peyretus has therefore asked his father for “sufragium vite sue.” Therefore, moved by paternal affection, Bernardus assigns to Peyretus the items listed in this inventory.

name: Inventory of Bartholomeus Egidii (ADBR 3B 62)
description: An ambassador has arrived from Pisa with a claim against the estate of Bartholomeus Egidii. A crier and a notary are sent to place a seal on several casks of wine in Bartholomeus's cellar and his wife is warned not to move the wine. Subsequently, an inventory is made of Bartholomeus's estate. Toward the end of the inventory, mention is made of the goods of Autrica, the wife of Bartholomeus, and Martileta, the wife of Johannes Egidi. It is likely that the women would be allowed to claim their dowry rights in the estate before the debt to the Pisan merchant could be honored.

name: Inventory of Johannes Johannis (ADBR 351E 17)
description: Alasacia, the widow of Johannes Johannes of Auriole, came to the court to declare the death of her husband and to register an inventory of his estate. The inventory includes very few goods.

name: Auction of Andreas de Septimis (ADBR 351E 258)
description: Very little context is provided for this act by means of which items formerly belonging to Andreas de Septimis were auctioned off at the request of Antonius Judi. The items consisted primarily of bedding; also sold was a measure and an agricultural implement. One possibility is that Andreas was a poor laborer living in a rented bedroom and that the items were sold off for unpaid rent.

name: Inventory of Guillelmus Ferrarii (AMM FF 501)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 501
description: Dulcia, the wife of Guillelmus Ferreri, seaman, citizen of Marseille, appeared in court. Guillelmus had died intestate, leaving behind his daughter and intestate heir, Hugueta, a baby girl aged 4 months. Hugueta doesn't have a guardian, so Dulcia requests one. The inventory has a number of interesting items, including two baskets from Sardinia and a Turkish carpet.

name: Auction of Rixendis Cambale (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Rixendis Cambale, one of Marseille's great women-merchants, died earlier in the year 1410, having outlived her son, Jacmetus Niel. Rixendis left her large estate to her granddaughter, Jacmetus's daughter, a girl named Jacmoneta Niella. Raymundus de Syon served as Jacmoneta's guardian. Immediately following the compilation of the inventory of Rixendis's estate, he proceeded, with the consent of the judge, to auction off the assets. This auction identifies goods by name, the purchaser, and the sale price. The auction has not been transcribed, and is made available here for individuals who wish to compare it with Rixendis's inventory, available in the DALME collection.

name: Inventory of Astrug Mosse (ADBR 3B 128)
description: This inventory records the possessions of a Jew named Astrug Mosse, a resident of the city of Marseille, who died on Wednesday, the 18th of July, 1397, without having made a will. Astrug had two daughters and intestate heirs named Venguesseta and Stereta, both of whom were under twenty years of age. The sisters chose to enter into the inheritance with benefit of inventory since there was some concern about whether the estate's debits might exceed its assets. In such an event, they could repudiate the estate rather than accept its debts. Too young to represent their interests in court, they asked the judge to assign them a guardian, naming for the role their cousin, Boniaquet Cohen. Boniaquet, who was present at the hearing, swore on the Mosaic law to serve honorably and was accepted by the judge. The compilation of the inventory was scheduled for Friday the 27th of July, and a crier issued a summons to the estate's creditors to attend the event if they so desired. On Friday, at vespers, the two sisters appeared at court, absent any creditors, and were allow to register the inventory they had made. At this point, they either transmitted a hand-list of the goods, written out in Provençal, or read the document out loud to the notary of the court, Peire Calvin. Either way, the notary probably translated the document into Latin on the spot; this is suggested by the presence of a number of corrections in the original. As was customary, the procedure commenced with the sign of the cross, although the document does not describe who made the sign. On the final folio, the sisters requested that an instrument of the act be made for them. The act gives no sign that the sisters were planning on repudiating the inheritance. Originally transcribed by Juliette Sibon, with corrections by D. Smail.

name: Inventory of Astrug de Aubenas and his wife Genseta (ADBR 3B 79)
description: Acquire images.

name: Inventory of Petrus Ferraudi (ADBR 355E 309)
description: This is not an inventory per se, it is an estima, or transfer of goods arising from insolvency. It includes a loose sheet containing the text of the estima in Provençal. The act was executed on behalf of Katherina, wife of Petrus Ferraudi, in order to allow her to recover her dowry of 100 florins.

name: Inventory of Bertrandus Tornatoris (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Jacmeta, wife of Bertrandus Tornatoris, appears before the court. She requests that the estate of her insolvent husband, Bertrandus, be evaluated by the city's estimators and that assets be awarded to her amounting to the value of her dowry of 70l. plus  expenses of 3l., equivalent in value to 43 florins and 9 gros. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: Inventory of Vivaudus de Jerusalem (AMM 1 II 44)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 44
description: The noblewoman Deodella, widow of the noble squire Vivaudus de Jerusalem, son of the late Vivaudus de Jerusalem, appears in court, and declares herself to be the guardian for Biatriseta, the couple's daughter, who is his heir. The girl is one year old. This is not an extremely wealthy inventory, given the decedent's standing, but it includes a number of interesting items, including two beds described as the servants'.

name: Codicil of Laureta de Rabesio (ADBR 392E 3)
description: This act is a codicil to a testament created by Laureta de Rabesio. See Laureta's inventory in the DALME collection.

name: Inventory of Johannes Arnaudi (ADBR 355E 1)
description: This is the inventory of Johannes Arnaudi, a baker, who died in the Black Death. He had named Gauzente and Pascal de Brinonia as his heirs. A curious phrase indicates that a different inventory could not be made on account of the absence of officers.

name: Inventory of Petrus Fresquerie (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Johanneta Saure, widow of the notary Petrus  Fresquerie, is seeking to recover her  dowry of 1000 florins and additional debts owed to her by the estate of her late husband. The total comes to 1522fl. 6gr. and she ends up receiving 1029fl. 11 gr. 1 quartum. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items. This inventory includes several extremely valuable garments.

name: Inventory of Margarita Massaribas (ADBR 351E 95)
description: No context is provided for the inventory of Margarita Massaribas.

name: Inventory of Crescas Rogeti (ADBR 3B 128)
description: acquire images

name: Inventory of Beatrix Ruffe (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Beatrix Ruffe appears in court and explains that her husband Arnulphus Ruffi, a carpenter, died intestate, leaving their children without a guardian. The children are Johannetus, age 18; Catherineta, the wife of Bertrandus Bedoyni, age 22; Dalfineta, age 8; Bertrandeta, age 4; and Bartholomayreta, age 8 months. She requests permission to appoint a guardian and to make an inventory of the estate. Beatrix is assigned as guardian, and her son Johannetus also makes an appearance. The inventory is extensive and includes the tools in the workshop of Arnulphus.

name: Inventory of Johannes de Favacio (ADBR 3 HD H 8)
parent_name: Archives départementales des Bouches-du-Rhône, Charter 3 HD H 8
description: Marquesius de Favacio appears in court as brother and  heir of the late  Johannes de Favacio and as the guardian for the siblings Jacobus de Favacio et  Dulcieta de Favacio, the children of the late Bernardus de Favacio  junior, who also share in the inheritance. Also appearing is Guillelmus de Favacio, another brother and co-heir of the late Johannes. They explain to the judge that Johannes de Favacio died in the recent plague, having left a testament in which he named his brothers, his nephew, and and his niece as his universal heirs, and they wish to conduct an inventory. Among other things, it includes an extensive list of fabric and their  prices per cane as well as several rain hats, a chain for tying up the  dog, and a child's tunic. The inventory was originally transcribed by Christine Barnel with corrections and additions by D. Smail. Bibliography Ripert, Laurent, Christine Barnel, Henri Bresc, Pascal Herberth, and Florence Colin, eds. Matériaux pour l’étude de la vie domestique et de la culture matérielle en Provence aux derniers siècles du Moyen Age. Razo (Nice). Cahiers du centre d’études médiévales de Nice 13. Pp. 58-62. Nice, France: Université de Nice, 1993. Barnel, Christine. “Les boutiques des frères Favas: drapiers et draperie à Marseille au XIVe siècle.” Provence Historique 49 (1999): 61–78.

name: Inventory of Poncius Gassini (ADBR 3B 57)
description: Poncius Gassini is the guardian for his niece Sibileta. He killed Alasacia Morgona and was sentenced by the criminal court to the loss of all his goods. Since Sibileta's assets are caught up in his, an inventory of the estate is ordered. The estate is large, and includes five agricultural properties and two houses. Some of the goods have been lost owing to humidity.

name: Inventory of Catharina Raynauda (ADBR 351E 195)
description: We have very little information about the context for the making of this inventory other than the fact that the goods are located in the house of Catherina Raynaude (and presumably are hers) and that the individual who compiled the inventory was Helia Boneti, a doctor of laws.

name: Inventory of Jacmeta de Apulea (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Jacmeta de Apulea died intestate, and there has been a dispute over her estate. This act opens when the jurist Paulus Triboleti and the notary Antonius Gumberti, the latter of whom is acting in the name of his wife Polheta, come before the judge to report that their adversary has been declared to have no rights in Jacmeta's estate. Having been placed in control of the property, they now wish to undertake an inventory and ask the permission of the court. The estate consists almost entirely of property. Near the end, an unusual phrase, crossed out in the MS, indicates that Jacmeta's husband had removed all of the assets from her residence before the compilation of the inventory.

name: Inventory of Jacobus de Jerusalem (ADBR 351E 87)
description: Jacobus de Jerusalem died, and there was a dispute over his estate setting his sister, Sicilia de Jerusalem, a nun of the monastery of Artecella near Aix-en-Provence, against Boniventa, his widow, who subsequently married Johannes Raynaudi, a licentiate in laws. Owing to the intervention of the abbot of Saint-Victor, the two women agreed on a compromise whereby they would split the estate evenly. The estate includes two houses although these are not listed in the inventory of the goods per se. On fol. 99r, these houses are valued together at 865 florins, which is a very substantial amount. The inventory includes separate rubrics for the decedent's clothing, which is highly unusual.

name: Inventory of Hugueta Biarde (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Bartholomea, the wife of Anthonius Tapoli, a butcher of Marseille, appeared in court, together with Johannes and Petrus Tapoli, the sons and heirs of Bartholomea and Antonius. They explained that domina Hugueta Biarde, the sister of Bartholomea, had died recently and made them her heirs. One of the interesting features of the inventory is that it describes a very limited array of kitchen items, consisting of a small broken cooking pot, a laundry basket, five barrels, a bread-basket, a small table, a flour-sieve, a copper pan, an iron frying pan, and a small tripod.

name: Inventory of Anthonius Bermundi (ADBR 3B 135)
description: Very little information is given about the context for this inventory of the goods of Antonius Bermundi, an urban peasant. In addition to a storeroom, the house had a bedroom with a bed as well as a modest assortment of kitchen wares. No clothing was found, suggesting that Antonius, like many relatively poor individuals, possessed a single set of garments that he wore every day. Like many peasants, Antonius invested in landholdings rather than movable goods.

name: Inventory of Guillelmus Martini (AMM 1 II 27)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 27
description: This lengthy record describes an inheritance dispute pitting Petrus Martini against the wife and young children of his deceased brother Guillelmus Martini. Their father, also named Guillelmus Martini, was a shipwright. Something about Bruneti; something about an avium maternum who is guardian of Jacmetus Johanneti and Jacmeta, siblings, children and heirs of Guillelmus Martini.

name: Dowry of Narbona wife of Mosse (ADBR 355E 84)
description: Bonsenhor Maravini and his son Mosse, Jews of Marseille, acknowledged having received a dowry from Narbona, the wife of Mosse, amounting to 150 florins in clothing, jewel, and money. In this act, Narbona acknowledged having received the goods listed here as compensation or security for her dowry. This list includes one of the most expensive articles of clothing from Marseille in this period, a cloak made of a scarlet fabric with adornments valued at 24 gold florins.

name: Inventory of Jacobus Iacobi (ADBR 351E 156)
description: This inventory appears to be the result of a criminal inquest against Jacobus Iacobi, who may have abandoned his goods and fled the city when charged with a crime. Since he may have taken more valuable things with him in his flight, this does not represent the contents of a typical poor household.

name: Inventory of Guillelmus Naulonqui (ADBR 381E 45ter)
description: Guillelmus Naulonqui, a carpenter, the son of Peire Naulonqui, has died, leaving behind Peyretus, age 15 years, Biatriseta, age 11 years, and Monetus, age 5 years. His wife Johaneta de Dia wishes to make an inventory of his estate.

name: Inventory of Simon Augerii (AMM 1 II 61)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 61
description: Simon Augerii and his wife Franqua died during the Black Death. At the time, they were living in the house of Anthonius Lurdi, located in a neighborhood known as the Lansaria. Simon died intestate, leaving no heirs or relatives closer in kinship than Albertinus Sanchonis, his nephew or "felezenus." No one, however, appears to know Albertinus's whereabouts. For this reason, his aunt, Francesquina de Noseu, wife of Paganicus de Noseu, compiles an inventory of the estate of the deceaased couple. The estate is not extensive but it includes some interesting items, including ceramics thought to be from the North African city of Bougie.

name: Inventory of Gauterius Duranti (AMM 1 II 21)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 21
description: Beatrix is the wife of the late Gauterius Duranti and the guardian for her children Hugueta, aged 11 years,  Guillelmeta, aged 9 year, and Gaverius?, aged 5 years. She appears in court and requests an inventory of the estate. This is a very rudimentary estate and the inventory offers insights into the lives of the poor.

name: Inventory of Bartholomeus (AMM 1 II 21)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 21
description: This document consists of a list of objects belonging to Bartholomeus, an otherwise unidentified individual who was presumably a member of the clergy. Owing to damage in the top right-hand corner of the page, some elements of the proceedings are not clear. The act mentions Guillelmus de Florencia, sacristan; Guillelmus Bermundi de Nicia; and Aymo de Bardegalis, judge of the Praepositura. Expenses described at the end indicate that the inventory arose from a bankruptcy proceeding.

name: Inventory of Jacobus Sialle (ADBR 3B 50)
description: Johannes and Henricus Syalhe, the sons of the late Jacobus Syalhe, appeared in court. Since they are between 14 and 25 years of age, and since they have pending lawsuits, they ask the judge to provide them with a guardian. The judge assigns Primarcus Mirapiscis as their guardian. The estate is burden with debts, notably to their mother for her dowry. Only houses and bastidas are listed in the estate; no goods are found.

name: Inventory of Hugo Boerii (ADBR 351E 17)
description: Jacoba, the widow of Hugo Boeri of the castrum of Auriol, appears in court. She explains to the bailiff that Hugo has died, leaving behind three daughters, Jacobeta, Anthoneta and Cannadeta. She asks permission to conduct an inventory of the estate. Like many inventories from country-folk, this one includes extensive properties but not much in the way of goods.

name: Inventory of Guillelmus Bertrandi (ADBR 3B 145)
description: Margarita, the widow of Guillelmus Bertrandi, a carpenter, appear in court. Her husband has died intestate, and she is seeking a guardian for their children, Messenona, 6 years old, and Antoneta, 3 years old. She is unwilling to serve as guardian and recommends Michael Bertrandi, the son of the late Guilhem, presumably by a different mother. Michael is present but says that he cannot serve as guardian for the children since he is engaged in litigation against the children by reason of Michael’s mother’s dowry and also his own wife’s dowry. A nobleman, Anthonius de Rocaforti, is eventually named guardian. The inventory is extensive.

name: Inventory of Martinus Milherie (ADBR 351E 203)
description: Catherina, the widow of Martinus Milherie, appears in court. She explains that her husband has died, leaving a testament in which he named as his heirs his children Peyronus, Johanonus, and Bernardeta. Catherina is named as their guardian.

name: Inventory of Johanneta Durelle (ADBR 351E 98)
description: NA

name: Inventory of the shop of Batrona Maurella (ADBR 351E 241)
description: This is the inventory of the apothecary shop of Batrona Maurella, widow of Gabriel Maurel. The date is uncertain although the year is clearly 1428.

name: Inventory of Sibilia Peyrone (ADBR 351E 133)
description: Sibilia Peyrone of Caderia, the daughter of Johannes Peyreri, is a resident of Marseille. Owing to her great affection for Peyretus Odolo of Saint-Maximin, she has chosen to donate all her movable and immovable goods to him to acknowledge the many services he has provided her. He in turn promises to manage the estate and to honor and provide for her. It is also part of the agreement that he cannot sell, donate, or alienate the estate without her permission.

name: Inventory of Jacobus Trelhe (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Jacobus Trelhe, a merchant, died on the last day of August 1410, naming Aycardona, his widow, as his heir. She is the daughter of Petrus Augelerii. Among other interesting items, the inventory includes a painted canvas or cloth (telam pictam) that was mounted on the wall behind the dining table. The inventory also lists the bedroom of the slave (camera serve), a very unusual reference in Marseille inventories. Jacobus and Aycardona possessed an exceptionally interesting set of clothing and a chest crafted in the Pisan style.

name: Dowry of Hugueta Blancherie (ADBR 355E 84)
description: NA

name: Inventory of Stephanus Civate (Blancard ed.)
parent_name: Documents inédits sur le commerce de Marseille au Moyen Age
description: This inventory records the estate of the draper, Stephanus Civate, on behalf of his son and heir, Stephanetus. Edited in: Louis Blancard, ed. Documents inédits sur le commerce de Marseille au Moyen Age. 2 vols. (Marseille: Barlatier-Feissat, 1884), vol. 2, pp. 403-415. Archival reference provided by Blancard: Archives de Marseille, notaire I, premier register de Guillaume Feraud, fol. 7v.

name: Inventory of Johannes Pico (ADBR 351E 171)
description: In this act, Johannes de Pahernis, the vice-jailer of the city, acknowledges to the smith Johannes Pico alias "Ayno" and Leoneta his wife that he has received the following goods in comanda. The items include Leoneta's dowry goods. This act is serving as a deposit or a temporary guardianship over the goods.

name: Inventory of Sibinde Cuende (AMM 1 II 7)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 7
description: Bertrandus Aymerici appears in court and announces that Sibinda Cuende, widow of the late Bernardus Cuendi, a shoemaker, has died, leaving a testament in which she named Bertrandus as her universal heir. He declares his intention of accepting the inheritance with benefit of inventory. Also available for consultation is Sibinda's testament. The inventory includes several instruments of credit indicating that Sibinda was a part-time moneylender.

name: Inventory of Anthonius Robaudi (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Anthonius Robaudi, a fishmonger, has died, and his wife Dulcia is seeking to recover her dowry of 300l. She has already been assigned 40l. of alimony, including 8l. expenses. She and her husband together owed 100fl. to Gabrielis Vassali, which she paid off, and she adds that sum. The total owed to her is 508 pounds, and with expenses (including funeral expenses) the sum comes to 586l. 16s. The goods are worth 536l. 8s. The immovable wealth is worth 122l. The movable goods are therefore worth 414l. 8s. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: Inventory of Antonius Bellipili (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Bertrandus Bellipili, son and coheir of Antonius Bellipili, an urban peasant, appears in court,  and presents a petition to the judge. Bertrandus explains that his father died recently, having left a testament written by Michael Folchalchi, notary. In the testament, the late Antonius named Bernardus and Ludovicus, his sons, as heirs. Bertrandus asks permission to be put in possession of the goods. There is some question of debts toward creditors. Owing to a dispute between the heirs, there is a delay in processing the request. Ultimately, the inventory is drawn up and the heirs divide the estate.

name: Inventory of Laureta de Rabesio (ADBR 3B 145)
description: Dulcieta Atulfa was the beneficiary of a donation of all the goods belonging to the late Laureta de Rabesio. Dulcieta wishes to have an inventory made of the goods. Both women bear the surnames of two of Marseille's distinguished families, and in part for this reason it is surprising that Laureta's assets are so rudimentary. One of the items kept in the kitchen, an oratory to the Virgin Mary, suggests that Laureta engaged in voluntary poverty for devotional reasons. For more background, see the codicil to Laureta's testament in the DALME collection.

name: Inventory of Gabriellus de Nantis (ADBR 351E 169)
description: This is an inventory for the shoemaker Gabriellus de Nante of Marseille. We know little about the context other than the fact that the request came from the chancery of Aix-en-Provence. The estate includes two houses and a oratory for the Blessed Mary, but otherwise is not well off.

name: Inventory of Guillelmus Gasanhi and Stevenetus Gasanhi (ADBR 351E 216)
description: Julianus Calvi, an urban peasant of Marseille, acknowledges to Guillelmus Gasanhi that he has received in comanda the goods listed below. The contract identifies an estate division involving Guillelmus and his nephew, Stevenetus Gasanhi.

name: Inventory of Mayer, son of Joseph Astrug (ADBR 3B 46)
description: Transcribed by Juliette Sibon. Acquire images. Begins fol. 144r. Le 27 juillet 1346. Vers primes. En présence du juge P. Malut, Douce, veuve de Mayer, affirme que son mari est mort ab intestat en laissant un fils, Bonjuson, dont elle demande la co-tutelle avec Vital de Largentière, son frère. Inventaire des biens du défunt fait par Douce :

name: Inventory of Johannes Isnardi de Sex Furnis (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Andriveta, widow of Johannes Isnardi de Sex  Furnis, is seeking to recover a dowry of 100l. (62.5 florins) as well as medical and funerary expenses. She paid expenses and medicines of 20 florins, 9 gros, and 2 quarter-gros. The total debt claimed is 98 florins, 3 gros, and 2 quarter-gros. The estate is valued at 109 florins and 11 gros and the boat and house together are worth 80 florins, so only 29 florins and 11 gros are in the goods. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: Inventory of Nicolaus Franchi (AMM 1 II 44)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 44
description: Jacoba Francha, the daughter of the late Nicolaus Franchi, a merchant, and the widow of Egidius Griffeni appears in court. She explains that Nicolauetus Franchi, age 18, the son of the late Guillemus Franchi, Jacoba's brother, has died intestate without leaving any children to succeed him. Jacoba, his aunt, is his closest relative. Therefore, she requests to be put in possession of his goods.

name: Inventory of Bernardus Garnerii (ADBR 4HD B 70)
parent_name: Archives départementales des Bouches-du-Rhône, Charter 4 HD B 70
description: The inventory is partial, since the instrument is missing a number of leaves. Does not include lists of property.The inventory was originally transcribed by Christine Barnel with corrections and editions by D. Smail.BibliographyRipert, Laurent, Christine

name: Inventory of Jacobus Rogerii (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Batrona Rogeria, widow of Jacobus Rogerii,  butcher, is seeking to recover her  dowry of 216l. from the estate of her late husband, along with an additional sum of 52. This is not necessarily a complete inventory; aamong other things, there are no clothes. The total sum assigned here is 176fl. 5gr., i.e. almost exactly the amount assigned. Possibly a number of items were left out of the reckoning. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: Inventory of Bonafossius Boneti of Lunello (AMM 1 II 44)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 44
description: Bonetus Vitalis, a Jew originally from the town of Uzès but now a citizen and resident of Marseille, appears in court. He explains that he has been named as the guardian for Bonetus Bensegnori, the son and heir of Bonafossius Boneti  of Lunel and his wife Doneta, citizens and residents of Marseille, both of whom have died. Bonetus requests permission to undertake an inventory of the estate. The inventory includes a number of brightly colored clothes as well as a number of children's things. The inventory ends abruptly, and since no mention is made of a kitchen, it is possible that the act is incomplete.

name: Inventory of Petrus Audeberti (AMM 2 II 11)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Charter 2 II 11
description: This act, currently the earliest inventory in the Marseille collection, concerns the estate of the late Petrus Audeberti, husband of the late Ermessendis. Petrus had a son named Johannes, who married Garcendis, and together they had a child named Guillelmus. Johannes appears to have predeceased his father, and Guillelmus is therefore the heir of his grandfather Petrus. His guardians are his mother and Bernardus de Margaritis.

name: Inventory of Bertrandus de Serveriis (AMM 1 II 18)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 18
description: This loose sheet of paper records an estate inventory  in Provençal in three columns. It is likely that the list was set down by Hugo Michaelis, the individual who compiled the inventory. Hugo would have handed the sheet of paper over to the notary of the court, who then annotated it at the end in Latin. The annotation indicates that on the ides of July in 1317, Hugo Michaelis, the guardian of the abandoned goods and inheritance of  Bertrandus, appeared in court. Hugo explains that he made the inventory on the request of Ybelina, the wife of Bertrandus.

name: Inventory of Petrus Castanee (ADBR 355E 1)
description: No context is provided for this inventory of Petrus Castanee, who died in the middle of the Black Death in March of 1348. This is a lengthy and interesting inventory.

name: Inventory of Petrus Saturnini (ADBR 351E 133)
description: Petrus Saturnini has died, leaving a testament in which he named his wife Gabriela as the guardian for their children. Gabriela appears in court and requests permission to compile an inventory. A notary accompanies Gabriela to their house in the carreria Jusatarie.

name: Inventory of Augerius Bote (AMM 2 II 221)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Charter 2 II 221
description: Jacobus Alvernhacii is the guardian for Jacmetus Bote, the son and heir of late Augerius Bote and the late Aynesia. He comes before the court and explains that Augerius died not long ago, and he requests permission to conduct an inventory of the estate so that he can manage it with benefit of inventory. This inventory, and probably this very same instrument, is referred to in the inventory of Johannes Casse, to whom some of the property listed in this inventory appears to have descended.

name: Inventory of Guillelmus Vesini (ADBR 3B 145)
description: In his testament dated 14 October 1402, Guillemus named Peyretus Vesini, his son, as his universal heir. His wife Garcendis was named as the guardian of the estate. She wishes to take up the inheritance with benefit of  inventory.

name: Dowry of Ayneseta Fabressa (ADBR 351E 137)
description: Ayneseta, daughter of the late Petrus Fabri and his wife Rixendis, married Nicolauetus Fabri, a fisherman, on 1 February 1392. In the dowry contract, goods and property valued at 240 l. were assigned to him. Ayneseta has been infirm for many years, however, and Nicolauetus has had to travel abroad on business in order to make a living. It appears that tensions have arisen between the couple, resulting in an act of arbitration. As a result of the arbitration, Nicolauetus, in this act, consigns ownership of goods and property to his wife for the necessary amount. At the end of the act, Ayneseta and her mother declare that the debt has been acquitted.

name: Inventory of Catharina Bollegone (ADBR 351E 179)
description: A rubric that is canceled suggests that the goods listed in this inventory belong to Catherine Bollegone. They are in the house of Johannes Martini, her son-in-law.

name: Inventory of Sileta Lhautaude (ADBR 351E 211)
description: Very little context is provided for the compilation of this inventory. The late Sileta was the wife of the late Monnetus Lautaudi, a seaman of the city. Her brother is Anthonetus Garini; also present is Johannetus Pellisserii, seaman,  her daughter Catherineta, and other individuals. The estate includes some interesting jewels and coins.

name: Inventory of Bermona Ruffa (AMM 1 II 44)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 44
description: Petrus de Antibolo appears in court and explains to the judge that Bermunda Ruffe has recently died, and during her final illness she executed a testament in which she named Petrus as her heir. He requests permission to undertake an inventory of the estate. The estate, which is not extensive, includes a spinning wheel and ten small Sardinian cheeses.

name: Inventory of Allays Gasc (AMM 1 II 18)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 18
description: The inventory was made at the request of Johan Gasc, Luin Gasc, and Martin Gasc, sons and heirs of Allays Gasc. The document, written in Provençal, is damaged and extremely difficult to read. The Provençal words used are unusual, compared to similar Provençal records from later in the fourteenth century, and for that reason the document is unusually important and merits more careful study. It is also one of the earliest inventories laid out in tabular format.

name: Inventory of Rixendis Calverie (ADBR 351E 240)
description: Domina Cardona Scandalhe, with the permission of Petrus Garrigue, her husband, acknowledges to Catherine, her daughter, the heir of domina Rixendis Calverie, widow of Johan de Bosco alias Barbavarie, that she received from her the hospicium that the testatrix left. The house is located in the carreria Nicolay Benaiga. She also receives all garments, both linen and woolen, both for daily wear and for festival occasions.

name: Inventory of Nicholaus Stornelli (AMM 4 II 28)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Charter 4 II 28
description: Johannes Elie, acting as a relative and representative of Jacobus Stornelli, co-heir of the late noble Nicolaus Stornelli, appears in court, along with Egidius Augilerii, the husband of Receneta, who is also a co-heir of Nicolaus. The two men wish to take up the inheritance with benefit of inventory. The estate is not exceptionally important but it includes a number of interesting things, including several paternosters made of coral and silver. Note that a testament left by a Nicolaus Stornelli is available in the DALME library, although the testament is from much earlier, 1355, suggesting that there are two individuals.

name: Inventory of Petrus Baboti (ADBR 351E 95)
description: Acting on the orders of a judge, two agents of the court put Johannona, widow of Petrus Baboti, in corporal possession of two houses belonging to her late husband. The act also lists several items pertaining to the estate.

name: Auction of the goods of Catherina Lumbarde (AMM FF 591)
parent_name: Archives Municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 591
description: Laurencius Bernardi, a merchant, appeared in court to explain that Catherina Lumbarde was indebted to him in the amount of 5 gold florins and 8 silver gros, arising from unpaid rent on a house. Some of Catherina's belongings were distrained and she was ordered to redeem them, if she wished, within a certain time period. Since she failed to do so, Laurencius requested permission to take possession of the items and auction them off to the highest bidder. The judge granted the request, and a notary of the court, accompanied by a crier, went to the house to seize the goods. During or following the auction, the notary redacted the inventory included here, identifying the purchaser, the object, and the price fetched.

name: Testament of Nicolaus Stornelli (AMM 4 II 44)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Charter 4 II 4
description: Testament of Nicolaus Stornelli, from 1355. See the 1389n inventory of Nicolaus Stornelli elsewhere in the DALME collection. There is an unusual gap between the dates, so it is possible that the two individuals are unrelated.

name: Inventory of Guillelmus Gaufridi (ADBR 351E 144)
description: This is the inventory of Guillelmus Gaufridi, an urban peasant; the context is not given.

name: Inventory of Guillelmus Pichoni (ADBR 355E 1)
description: This is an inventory for the late Guillelmus Pichoni, who died at the height of the Black Death in March of 1348. Little context is provided in the act itself, although we know from other sources that he was a draper. His wife was named Alaseta and he had two daughters, Catherina and Johanna, the latter of whom was a nun.

name: Inventory of Fulco Amati (ADBR 3B 32)
description: Francisca, the widow of Fulco Amati, appeared in court along with their sons Peyretus, aged 17, Jacmetus, aged 11, Cabriel, aged 9, and Marcellona, aged 6. Fulco had died intestate in Naples, leaving his children as his heirs. They have no guardian. The record opens with several folios that record the judicial proceedings, and the inventory begins on folio 20r.

name: Inventory of Guillelmus de Cavallione (ADBR 3B 145)
description: Jacobus Guillelmi appears in court on behalf of his sister, Lady Massileta, widow of Guillelmus de Cavallione, and requests an inventory of the estate. The items include a parrot's cage.

name: Inventory of Nadala Raymunde (ADBR 351E 220)
description: Lying ill in bed, Nadala Raymunde, the widow of the late Anthonius Raymundi, an urban peasant, is making her testament so as to avoid any disputes among her heirs. Unusually,  she chooses to include a list of her assets.

name: Inventory of Anthonius Boneti (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Anthonius Boneti, an apothecary, is bankrupt and his wife Johaneta is seeking to recover her dowry of 100 florins and an additional sum of 4 florins, plus expenses, from his estate. The resulting inventory provides a room-by-room description of the house, including interesting line-item references to the spices and other products in his shop. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: Inventory of Petrus Melerii (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Hugueta, wife of Petrus Melerii, is seeking to recover a dowry of 34l. (21fl. 2gr.) The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: List of objects of Hugo de Sancta Maria (AM FF 532)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 532
description: This is a fragmentary list of objects from a court case in 1353 that appears to involve Hugo de Sancta Maria.

name: Inventory of Ricardus Jullani (AMM FF 501)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 501
description: Gayranna, the mother of the late Ricardus Jullani, appeared in court to request permission to register the inventory of her son's estate. Ricardus had died some time earlier, leaving six children. In his testament,he assigned certain sums of money to his daughters Jacmeta and Aycardeta, and named his sons Giraudetus, Jacmetus, Peyretus, and Raymundetus as his universal heirs in equal parts. In the testament, he also named his widow Raymunda as the children's guardian. The inventory recorded here was occasioned by the fact that Raymunda had decided to marry again and  was  no longer able to serve as the children's guardian. Gayranna therefore requested that she be named as  guardian along with Poncius de Sancto Martino. This is a remarkable inventory of the shop of an apothecary and a general merchandiser who specialized in the coral trade. The register has been damaged by book lice and humidity, and expert analysis will improve the first-pass transcription that we make available here. A partial transcription, including a glossary, is available in G. D’Agnel and Émile Isnard, “Inventaires de mobiliers provencaux du XIIIe siècle tirés des archives de Marseille,” Comité des Travaux Historiques et Scientifiques, Bulletin Archéologique 1 (1914): 103–105.

name: Inventory of Raymundus de Buco (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Catherina, the widow of Raymundus de Buco, a cord-maker, appeared in court and declared that her husband died recently, leaving a testament in which he named his three sons and daughter as his universal heirs. He also named Catherina as the children's guardian. This is a well-to-do household, and includes some very interesting references to raw materials used for making cords and belts. Transcriber: Juliette Calvarin

name: Inventory of Rixendis Cambale (ADBR 355E 309)
description: This is an act of guardianship for Jacmoneta, daughter of the late Jacmetus Nielli and Alaxieta, now the wife of Raymundus de Syon, merchant of Marseille. The guardianship concerns the estate that Jacmoneta has inherited from the late Rixendis Cambale, one of Marseille's great women-merchants. Immediately after the inventory was made, portions of Rixendis's estate--primarily worn or cheap kitchenwares and linens--were auctioned off piecemeal to the highest bidders (the auction is available in the DALME collection). The estate includes many items bearing the arms of Johannes Nielli, the girl's grandfather and Rixendis's late husband, as well as an extensive list of items in the apothecary's shop belonging to the family business. It is one of the rare inventories from Marseille to mention relics.

name: Inventory of Hugua (ADBR 351E 124)
description: Very little context is provided for this inventory of a woman named Hugua.

name: Inventory of Bertrandus Marini (AMM FF 501)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 501
description: Three women appear in court: Marina de Castellana, wife of the late Petrus de Castellana; Garcia, wife of Petrus Berrerii; and  Garcendis, wife of the late Bertrandus Arnulfi. They explain that their father Bertrandus Marini has died, having left a testament in which he named his three daughters as his heirs. They wish to take up the estate with benefit of inventory. The inventory was originally transcribed by Christine Barnel with corrections and addtions by D. Smail. Bibliography: Ripert, Laurent, Christine Barnel, Henri Bresc, Pascal Herberth, and Florence Colin, eds. Matériaux pour l’étude de la vie domestique et de la culture matérielle en Provence aux derniers siècles du Moyen Age. Razo (Nice). Cahiers du centre d’études médiévales de Nice 13. Pp. 47-48. Nice, France: Université de Nice, 1993.

name: Inventory of Isnardus Raymbaudi (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Sibilia, widow of Isnardus Raymbaudi, jurist,  is seeking to recover a dowry of 300 florins. The house is worth 62fl. 6gr. She is still owed 181fl. 5gr. 3q. Apparently she received 121 fl. 6gr. and 1q. The goods are therefore worth 59fl. and 1q. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: Inventory of Victor de Massello (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Lady Hugeta is seeking to recover her dowry of 160l. from the estate of her late husband, Victor de Massello. The total with expenses is 113fl. 11gr. 1q. The total value of estate is the same. Land is worth 81fl.; goods worth 32fl. 11gr. 1q. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: Inventory of Mosse Creguti (ADBR 3B 145)
description: Arfila, the widow of Mosse Creguti, appeared in court. She explained that the late Mosse died intestate not long ago, leaving his sons Salvetus and Astruguetus as his presumptive heirs. Sensing that the estate was burdened with debts, however, they chose to repudiate it. What emerges from the subsequent proceedings is that the estate is obligated to Arfila for her dowry of 40 florins. Master Abraam de Mayranicis, a physician, was named as guardian for the undefended estate. The inventory compiled by Abraam has a number of interesting objects, including three books written in Hebrew, a rooster, and three hens.

name: Inventory of Biatrix Martina (ADBR 351E 222)
description: Biatrix, the widow of a plasterer named Johannes Martini, is suffering from an unspecified illness. She is giving all her goods in comanda to her son, magister Aycardus Martini, her son. He promises to restore the goods when asked. A note at the end indicates that Biatrix survived and recovered her goods.

name: Inventory of Berengarius de Bulbono (AMM 2 II 291)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Charter 2 II 291
description: Johannes de Monteolivo, of Arles, appears in court. He explains that Berengarius de Bulbono, knight, died recently, having left a testament in which he named Johannes as his heir. Johannes intends to take up the inheritance with benefit of inventory. A notary of the court was asked to go to Berengarius's house so as to transcribe all the movables and immovables, and the creditors were invited to attend. The inventory is extensive and includes a number of unique objects, such as a bathtub designed for ladies and several items from the Barbary coast. The instrument ends abruptly, indicating that one or more leaves of parchment have been lost, although the list of assets shows every sign of drawing to an end. The photomerged image currently displayed has some errors. Also available for consultation in the DALME collection is the testament of Berengarius de Bulbono, although the text has not yet been transcribed. The inventory was originally transcribed by Christine Barnel with corrections and editions by D. Smail.BibliographyRipert, Laurent, Christine Barnel, Henri Bresc, Pascal Herberth, and Florence Colin, eds. Matériaux pour l’étude de la vie domestique et de la culture matérielle en Provence aux derniers siècles du Moyen Age. Razo (Nice). Cahiers du centre d’études médiévales de Nice 13. Pp. 63-71. Nice, France: Université de Nice, 1993.

name: Inventory of Ugona Rebolla (ADBR 351E 203)
description: Hugoya, the widow of Hugo, appears in court with her sons Anthonius and Guilellmus. She claims that they are obligated to restore to her the movable goods and utensils that she brought with her into her marriage with Hugo.

name: Inventory of Arnulphus de Parisius (ADBR 351E 95)
description: This is the inventory of a priest or canon, probably associated with the cathedral church of Marseille, Beate Marie Sedis Massilie

name: Auction of goods of Antoneta Bonivine (ADBR 351E 172)
description: This acts, from March of 1420, presents a list of items belonging to Antoneta Bonivine which she had consigned to Fossetus Mahier on the understanding that he would auction them. The expectation is that the items would fetch 25 florins in toto, and Fossetus acknowledges owing this sum to Antoneta. A follow-up act from August of the same year indicates that the transaction was completed successfully. The items include three houppelandes and several other garments, and the presence of several arms suggests that these items had belonged to Antoneta's late husband Johannes. The foliation is uncertain

name: Inventory of Martha Flote (ADBR 351E 17)
description: This is a dowry act for Monnerius Pauli, alias Marini, formerly a resident of Auriol, and Martha Flote, daughter of the late Hugo Floti of the castrum. The dowry she assigns to her new husband includes what appears to be Martha's complete estate. The estate includes a silk veil or headdress (velum), which is unusual in rural areas.

name: Inventory of the priest Guillelmus Valencie (ADBR 5G 775)
description: Johannes Mounerii, jurist, procurator for the episcopal chapter, appears in court, along with Biatrix Gavota, wife and heir of Pauleti Laurencii. They explain that lord Guillelmus Valencie, a priest and beneficed cleric in the church of Marseille, has died, leaving a testament in which he declared Biatrix to be his heir for life. They request permission to conduct an inventory. The second half of the dossier, not yet read or analyzed, appears to consist of a set of accounts describing services provided by Guillelmus.

name: Inventory of Bertrandus Fulconis (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Guillelmus Fulconis, the cousin of Bertrandus Fulconis, laborer, appeared in court and declared that Bertrandus had died, naming Nicholaus, the son of Guillelmus, as his heir. He requests permission to make an inventory.

name: Inventory of Honoratus Bavili (AMM FF 591)
parent_name: Archives Municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 591
description: Lazaretus Raynoardi, a draper, and Astruguetus Salveti Tamerani, a Jew, appear before the judge. Honoratus Bavili, the son of the late notary Guillelmus Bavili, has been incarcerated for debts and both Lazaretus and Astruguetus, who are among Honoratus's creditors for 9 florins and 16 florins respectively, request the judge to prepare an inventory of his estate. They are concerned that goods might be removed from the house. The inventory is incomplete.

name: Inventory of Enricus Palmanayre (ADBR 355E 1)
description: This inventory, executed at the very height of the Black Death in April of 1348, was made for Laurencia Palmanayre, the widow of the late Enricus Palmanayre and guardian for Amadeta, their daughter, her husband's heir. We know from other sources that Enricus was a maker of sheaths or scabbards (gaynerius). His estate suggests a relatively modest economic standing--his house, for example, does not appear to have had many rooms--although he did possess four rural properties and was a winemaker. The estate included numerous arms and weapons.

name: Inventory of Jacobus de Landa (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: Catharina, wife of Jacobus de Landa, shoemaker, is seeking to recover a dowry of 100fl. and expenses of 3fl. 4gr. The goods only are worth 28fl. 2½gr. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: Inventory of Anthonius Bermundi (ADBR 3B 144)
description: Little context is provided for this record of the estate of Antonius Bermundi, who appears to have been in the wine-production business.. The items listed, which include several arms, are typical of a Provençal household at the time. One of the rooms, unusually, is identified as the bedroom of the servant.

name: Inventory of the goods of Johanneta Aymara (ADBR 351E 208)
description: Johanneta Aymara, a sex worker, drew up this inventory of the brothel she managed because she was about to set out on a pilgrimage to the shrine of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Le Puy. Shortly before departure, pilgrims often left their goods in the power of a trusted friend or relative, using a legal contract known as a "comanda." Comanda contracts were most commonly used for commercial investments, but they could also serve the needs of pilgrims as well, since they gave the temporary holder the ability to manage the goods for a profit. Upon the return of the pilgrim, the trusted friend would then restore the goods to the owner. Johanneta shared her house and assets with her concubinous partner, Johannetus Raynaudi, described in the record as her "amicus." The management of the goods listed in this inventory, however, was assigned to their servant, Anthonius Soquini, possibly because Johannetus was intending to go on pilgrimage as well. As suggested by the number of beds (four), this inventory describes a working brothel. The presence of spits, other cooking implements, tablewares, and twenty-seven amphorae indicates that Johanneta offered good food to her clients. Noteworthy is a retable (an image or a shrine) depicting the Blessed Virgin Mary. The witness list consisted of two associates of Marseille's "sub-vicar," an officer who can be considered the city's chief-of-police. One expects that they were among Johanneta's trusted clients.

name: Inventory of Guillelmus Broquerii (AMM 1 II 23)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 23
description: Succession and inventory for Guillelmus Broquerii, requested by his brother Hugo.Guillelmus, aged more than 25 years, Peyreonus, aged between 14 and 25 years, Duratonus, aged between 10 and 14 years, and  Johannetus, between 6 and 12 years. Berengaria is his widow. Hugo asks to be named guardian for his nephews.

name: Inventory of Fosse (ADBR 3B 150)
description: This is an inventory for the late Fossa, who died in the summer of 1412. Fossa may be the widow of Astruguet Ali alius Jossé, a coral fisherman. She appears in one other act from 1390. We know that Fosse had two daughters and a son, Astruga (who was the widow of Astrug, also a Jew), Anne, and Codolletus. The inventory was drawn up at the request of Codolletus on behalf of Anne, Fosse's only heir. The inventory is remarkable for the presence of Jewish devotional objects, many paternosters or rosaries, many objects made of coral, possessions held in pawn, precious jewels and silks, and articles of clothing described as specifically "Jewish."

name: Auction of miscellaneous goods (ADBR 3B 144)
description: A miscellaneous list of goods with their auction prices are found on these two folios. The parties involved include the nobleman Berengarius Vivaudi and a woman named Aycelena.

name: Inventory of Thomacius Blanquerii (ADBR 355E 1)
description: Jacoba Blanqueria, the daughter of Petrus de Brandisio and the wife of the late  Thomacius Blanquerii, appears in court. She explains that her husband died recently, leaving a daughter and heir, Bartholomea, who is a child and has not been provided with a guardian. As the child's mother and closest kin, she humbly requests that the guardianship be assigned to her. The judge complies, and Jacoba proceeds with the inventory.

name: Inventory of Johannes Molnerii (ADBR 351E 252)
description: A house and forge belonging to the late Johannes Borrelli, a smith, and his wife Francisca were sold at auction by order of the court of Marseille. The reason for the court-ordered sale is not given; it may relate to a criminal fine or bankruptcy. The property and its contents were subsequently purchased by Johannes Molnerii, an apothecary. Now, Johannes Molnerii is selling the property to the smith  Johannes Jauberti and his wife Hugona. The  purchasers are described as being from France and appear to be recent immigrants. For the house and forge, they agree to pay 96 florins of France, and for its contents, 20 florins and 8 gros. The total sum is 116 florins and 8 gros, and a plan is set up allowing the couple to pay in installments.

name: Inventory of the priest Raymundus Adsami (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: This is the inventory of the estate of the priest Raymundus Adsami, carried out at the request of Alasacia Adsame, wife of Guillelmus Fabri, and Petrus Boneti, his heirs.

name: Price list (ADBR 351E 198)
description: Although the context for this act is unclear, the list seems to describe goods that are being deposited or invested in an enterprise. Two Jewish assessors were paid to provide value estimates for the goods, consisting of beds, bed linens, tables, and kitchen furnishings.

name: Inventory of Sanxia Raolina (ADBR 3B 38)
description: This inventory arises from a very complex lawsuit that was initiated in July of 1339. Bartholomeus Martini senior had been married to a woman named Sanxia, and she bore two sons, Bartholomeus junior and Raolinus. Both sons got married, Bartholomeus to a woman named Francisca and Raolinus to Nicolaua. Fourteen years ago, Sanxia died, naming her two sons as her heirs, but granting her husband Bartholomeus senior usufruct of the inheritance for life. She herself had been the sole heir of her father Raymundus Raolini, so her estate was worth a great deal. After Sanxia's death, Bartholomeus senior married a woman named Nicolaua, and together they had children. Because he is old and senile, according his sons, they are concerned that the Raolini inheritance will go to his children by Nicolaua. Accordingly, they are taking steps to recover the Raolini estate from the estate of their father. In addition, their two wives are seeking to recover their dowries from the estate. Francisca's dowry is worth 300l., and Nicolaua's 600l. The entire case may be found in ADBR 3 B 38, folios 135r to 164r. The images provided here are limited to the signature containing the inventory, which was bound into the court register.

name: Inventory of Bertrandus de Vellancio (ADBR 351E 142)
description: This act records the estate inventory of a goldsmith named Bertrandus de Vellancio, executed by his wife Gassenda for their daughter whose name appears to be Constancia. Among other things, it includes some devotional items he was working on at the time of his death.

name: Inventory of Andreas de Garda (ADBR 392E 1)
description: Hugueta, the widow of the late fisherman Andreas de Garda, appeared in court, explaining that her late husband died the previous month, on the 7th of June, having left a testament in which he named Hugueta and their children, Jacmetum and Ludovicetum, along with his step-son, Bertrandus Radulphi, as his universal heirs. He had not made arrangements for the children's guardian, however, and Hugueta requested that she be named the children's guardian. This is a well-to-do estate of a fisherman which lists several fishing boats and a small inventory of nets with their Provençal names. Other interesting items include two fencing swords and an entry for apothecary's preparations taken by Andreas in his final illness.

name: Inventory of Rixendis Blanchana (AMM FF 501)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 501
description: Rixendis Blanchana has died, leaving a testament in which she named Olivarius, son of dominus Rollandus de Mari, as her heir. The estate included a house and a fairly undistinguished assortment of goods. An addendum listed some clothing not found in the original inventory.

name: Inventory of Narratus (ADBR 351E 152)
description: This inventory is found in a notarial register apparently containing miscellaneous court business, date uncertain

name: Inventory of Guillelma Ginhaque (ADBR 3B 41)
description: Guillelma is a debt-fugitive and has abandoned her assets to her creditors. See also the inventory of Raymundus Cabrerii in this collection.

name: Inventory of Antonius Stephani (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Antonius, a macellarius or butcher, died not long ago; he left a testament dated 1409, 21 March, and instituted as his universal heirs Pellegrinus and Fulquetus, his sons, in equal parts. Among the many interesting items in this inventory are two dog collars, a very rare instance of the material culture of dogs. The notary has carefully crossed out a series of "Items" in this inventory.

name: Inventory of Johannes de Bui or Macipetus Maurelli (ADBR 351E 152)
description: Very little context is provided for this inventory. It lists the assets of an individual who is being prosecuted for an unspecified crime. The date is uncertain. The previous page contains notes on two separate prosecutions, the first against a Christian named Johannes de Bui, and the second against a Jew named Macipetus Maurelli.

name: Inventory of Hugo Augerii (AMM 2 II 460)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Charter 2 II 460
description: Because the parchment recording this inventory is torn or damaged on the right-hand side, between five and eight words have been lost on each line. Even so, it is possible to make out some of the details. A woman named Alasacia Augeria, wife of Antonius Augerii, is concerned about the impending insolvency of the estate of her father-in-law, Hugo Augerii, alias Salinherii, an urban peasant. She describes how her dowry was assigned both to her father-in-law and her husband. She asks the city's bankruptcy court to assess the estate of her husband Antonius and to convey to her assets sufficient to repay her dowry of 56 florins. The act begins with a reference to Jacobus Jordani, Alexander Gomberti, and Bernardus de Conchis, who are in all likelihood the “extimatores generales” in charge of estimating the assets of insolvent estates and distributing the assets to the creditors.

name: Inventory of Jacobus Jugueti (AMM 1 II 44)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register 1 II 44
description: Jacobus de Niuzellis appears in court. He announces that Jacobus Jugueti, cobbler, has died, and in his testament named Jacobus de Niuzellis as his heir. He requests permission to compile an inventory.
