name: Inventory of Guillelmus Fayssati (ADBR 351E 98)
description: Honoratus Fayssati, son of the late Guillelmus Fayssati, a notary of Marseille, acknowledges to his mother Vivauda, daughter of the late Anthonius Bonifilii, that he has received the goods  on the ensuing list. He promises to restore the goods at her request. The context is uncertain.

name: Inventory of Poncius Barbessaure (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Domina Margarita, widow of the candler Poncius Barbessaure, appears in court with her son Honoratus. They explain that Poncius has died intestate. The couple's children, in addition to Honoratus, include Raymundus Barbessaure, prior of Saint-Nicolaus and monk of Saint-Victor, and Petrus and Nicholas, both of whom are serving in the army of the king. The inventory includes a number of tools-of-the-trade associated with making candles.

name: Inventory of Johannes Bermundi (ADBR 3B 61)
description: A young man named Johannes Bermundi has died from an illness, and his relatives are blaming each other for his death and fighting over his estate. In the midst of the lawsuit, it was felt necessary to draw up an inventory of his assets. The images and transcriptions provided here concern just the portion of the lawsuit where the inventory is drawn up.

name: Inventory of Johannes Ricavi (ADBR 355E 309)
description: Johannes died on 22 November 1410, having left a testament in which he named his son Gaspar as his heir. Gaspar appeared in court requesting permission to compile an inventory. The list of goods includes some green bed curtains depicting lilies and birds and a tapestry described as a "historiated cloth from France for hanging behind the dining table."

name: Inventory of Laurencius Vassalli (ADBR 3B 145)
description: Bertrandus Vassalli appears in court. He explains to the judge that his brother Laurencius has died, and that he was appointed by his late brother to be the guardian for Laurens’ son Guillelmetus Vassalli. He requests permission to undertake an inventory. The resulting inventory is extensive and has many interesting objects. Laurencius's testament is also available in the DALME collection though at present it has not been edited.

name: Inventory of Lazarus Spinelli (AMM FF 1009)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 1009
description: At the request of Nicolay de Arena, jurist, procurator for Johannes  Terrassanti and his associates of Albengona, the estimators of the  bankruptcy court are undertaking an evaluation of the assets of the  estate of the late Lazarus Spinelli, a cooper, in order to reimburse his creditors. Since other creditors step forward, including his daughter, this is a composite record consisting of four separate lists entered at different locations in the register. The inventory includes line-item estimates of the value of the items.

name: Inventory of Bertrana Caparrone (ADBR 351E 156)
description: Very little is known about the women, Bertrana Caparrone, whose estate is inventoried here. The document appears in a set of inventories generated by the criminal court, so it is possible that her assets were being seized for some unspecified crime. Her assets include two instruments describing debts owed to her.

name: Testament of Laurencius Vassalli (ADBR 392E 3)
description: This act records the last will and testament of Laurencius Vassalli. Consult his inventory in the DALME collection.

name: Inventory of Johannes Casse (AMM 3 II 40)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Charter 3 II 40
description: Johannes Casse was a very prominent merchant in the second half of the fourteenth century and died childless in 1391, leaving his estate to his second wife, Raynauda, for her life, and naming the Hospital of Saint-Jacques de  Galicia as the substitute heir upon her death. The inventory was partially transcribed and published in 1907 by Henri Villard (Jean Casse, armateur et marchand marseillais du XIV siècle: sa maison, son comptoire, sa bastide. Aix: Villard, 1907). The transcription provided here has been checked against the original parchment and corrected, and the elements left out by Villard, notably the debts, have been newly transcribed. The estate is interesting for the considerable number of devotional objects it contains, as well as the description it provides of Johannes's cartularies and instruments and the extensive volume of debts he owed. One of the entries refers to an instrument containing an inventory of an estate compiled on the behalf of Jacobus Bote in 1348. This refers to the inventory of Augerius Bote which may be viewed in the DALME collection, and it is not unlikely that the parchment inventory of the estate of Augerius Bote is the one that appears in the inventory of Joahnnes Casse.  The parchment includes an unusual number of emendations and notes.  As of January 2020, the charter image has been imperfectly photomerged; the DALME project will take appropriate steps soon to rectify the image at some point in the future.

name: Inventory of Raymundus Audeberti (AMM FF 501)
parent_name: Archives municipales de la ville de Marseille, Register FF 501
description: Hugua appeared in court to announce the death of her husband, Raymundus Audeberti, a laborator of Marseille. She requested permission to be named guardian for their children Vivaudeta, Alayzeta, and Jacmetus. The estate, like those of many urban peasants, displays a fairly rudimentary assortment of household things but is well-off in terms of vineyards and fields.
